source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #265 (branch fix/197-jit-relocations at merge commit 83d2372420ff675f2f6de3ec80d275a51dd745a1 — branch head 3646905ff2cd6780160184f70e95936aece61c46 with current main e91089baa9a889e83d2e615a5bf0dbed62addf87 merged in without conflicts, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45112476845 and 45112481681 against the branch and pull-request run 45112159380, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #265 (#197, record relocations in the JIT emitters). The PR generalises the three baseline JIT emitters over a monomorphised EmitEnv: the JIT implementation reproduces the previous behaviour from the live store, while the AoT implementation supplies recipes from the parsed Module and records stub addresses / funcaddr immediates as placeholders plus a relocation table (RelocKind::{Stub(StubId), FuncAddr(funcidx)}); the 44 stubs gain a single source of truth (StubId table + fingerprint), and the patcher rewrites each site at the same length after verifying the placeholder. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (e91089b) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45112486937, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. Only the core-jit configuration links telomere-jit-codegen and the JIT emitters into the minimal embedder, so the delta is confined to its four gated series: release stripped file +2,552 B / stripped .text +848 B; release-size stripped file +720 B / stripped .text −672 B (the release-size .text shrink is the code-layout effect of the emitter refactor under that profile’s optimisation settings, as in earlier re-baselines). The other 24 gated series are byte-identical. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
